# Seed-aware ring definitions source and id lookup

## Goal

Give every runtime consumer one seed-aware seam for "the definitions of this
ring" and "the definition of this hex id", so no consumer needs the authored
table and a looked-up hex always matches the ring the war is playing.

**User story:** As a test/agent, definition lookup by hex id is derivable from
the same seed as the ring, so intel, the special-mission rotation, the defence
resolver and the harness can never disagree about what a hex is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single pure source seam exists (e.g. `ringDefinitionsFor(seed, ringIndex)` and `findRingDefinition(seed, ringIndex, hexId)` exported alongside the generator) that returns the generated definitions for the war's `payload.seed`; every default currently reading `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` / `hexRingDefinitionsFor` / `findHexRingDefinition` is wired to it.
- Definition lookup by hex id is derived from the generated ring, not from a static table: `buildHexMapModel`, `specialMissionRingView` / `specialMissionOfferFor`, `authoredRingBaseMass` (and the `attackerType` boss lookup) and `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` all consult the seam and receive the same definitions the ring state was materialised from.
- An injected `definitions` option still wins over the default (tests and gym overrides keep working), and passing definitions for a different ring cannot leak into a lookup (the source is keyed by ring index).
- Any remaining import of authored ring content from a non-test, non-fixture module is removed; `grep` for `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` outside the retirement item's own cleanup finds no runtime consumer.
- Unit tests assert that intel, the special-mission rotation and the aggression base mass agree with the generated ring for several seeds and rings, including a ring index above 2.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- The seam takes the **seed** (a number), never the whole payload, so the core
  stays pure and a caller can resolve a future ring's intel without mutating
  state.
- A ring index above the old authored ceiling must already work here (the
  generator is the whole content source); the frontier/migration behaviour is
  the next item's concern.
- Do not delete `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` in this item — the retirement item owns
  that removal plus the fixture/scene/test migration, so this item can land
  green with the authored table still present but unused by the seams it owns.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — the generator and the new definitions-source exports.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — `buildHexMapModel` / `pickAttractHex` defaults and the by-id definition fallback.
- `src/core/hangarWar/specialMission.ts` — `specialMissionRingView` / `specialMissionOfferFor` defaults.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — `authoredRingBaseMass` and the defender `attackerType` boss lookup.
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HangarWarPayload.seed` (the generation seed source).
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` — the harness definitions lookup.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/specialMission.test.ts` — consumer agreement tests.

## Related work

- Parent **AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA** — Procedurally generated Hex Map (epic).
- **AH-0MVUXC9KG008G80Y** — origin of the by-id lookup and the authored table
  this seam replaces.
- **AH-0MWJ51KUS005WQK6**, **AH-0MWF0CTQB001XFE1** — special-mission hexes whose
  lookup must keep resolving.
- **AH-0MWHWF5D4000J0RB** — held-hex UPGRADE DEFENCES map action (blocked,
  tangential) consumes the map read model; the seam must not regress it.

# On-demand materialisation and an unlimited frontier

## Goal

Remove the authored-successor ceiling from ring progression: opening the next
ring generates it from the seed for **any** ring index, so a war never stalls.

**User story:** As a player, securing a ring always opens the next, bigger ring
— ring 3, ring 4 and beyond — because the successor is generated on demand
rather than waiting for authored data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `materialiseRing` generates the ring from `payload.seed` when the stored ring is empty (a fresh war) and returns a stored ring unchanged when it holds any hexes — never re-rolling, padding or discarding.
- `openNextRing` succeeds for every ring index from 1 upward (asserted through at least ring 10): it generates the successor ring from the seed, appends it to the carried hexes exactly as today, reports `opened: true` and the new `ringIndex`, and no longer leaves the ring secured because an authored successor is missing.
- Ring advancement is exercised end-to-end (secure or rush a ring → next ring opens → its hexes are displayable, capturable and taggable by intel) in an integration test that reaches at least ring 4.
- The aggression budget for a generated ring is derived from that ring's generated base mass (`authoredRingBaseMass` reads the same source as materialisation), so the frontier tick's mass, floor and beatable-hex guarantee hold for rings above 2.
- The `try`/`catch` around a missing authored ring in `createRingState` is replaced by generation for a positive ring index; a non-positive or corrupt ring index still degrades safely rather than throwing mid-render.
- Existing ring-advance behaviour is preserved: a rush past unheld hexes keeps those hexes (held state, defender, aggression) in the payload, and the ring-end hangar assault gate still runs before any advance.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- The stored-ring invariant is absolute: a non-empty `ring.hexes` array is never
  regenerated, so a save's seen map can never change under the player (see the
  save-compatibility item for the defensive-parse half).
- Rush/secure semantics are unchanged: only *where the successor content comes
  from* changes, not when a ring opens.
- This item may keep the authored table present (retirement is the following
  item) but must not require it to exist for progression.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — `materialiseRing`, `openNextRing`, `createRingState` call sites and the ring-advance result.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — `createRingState` gains the seed-aware generation path.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — `authoredRingBaseMass` / `ringAggressionBudget` feeding off the generated base mass.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.test.ts` — ring-advance and materialisation tests.
- `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/aggressionScenarios.ts` — the harness's synthesised "ring 3+" shape can now use the real generator.
- `src/scenes/hangarWarTraversal.integration.test.ts` — multi-ring traversal integration coverage.

## Related work

- Parent **AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA** — Procedurally generated Hex Map (epic).
- **AH-0MVXSHAS100010S0** — rush push into the next ring is playable (AC8 gap):
  the rush seam this item must not regress.
- **AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J** — the ring-end hangar assault gate that runs before
  any advance.
- **AH-0MWHWF5D4000J0RB** — held-hex UPGRADE DEFENCES map action (blocked,
  tangential): consumes the map read model.

# Retire the authored ring table and CSV seeds

## Goal

Complete the content migration: remove the authored runtime table and the CSV
seeds, and move every scene, fixture, harness and test to the generator —
rings 1 and 2 now generate from the seed like every other ring.

**User story:** As a designer, I no longer author a table per ring; the
generator is the single content source and nothing can drift from it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The authored runtime table `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` and the `hex-ring-1.csv` / `hex-ring-2.csv` seeds are **retired as the runtime content source** (no scene or runtime path imports authored ring content; the CSV parity test is removed or replaced), and rings 1 and 2 generate from the seed like every other ring.
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` is deleted or reduced to vocabulary re-exports only (no `HexRingDefinition` rows), `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv` / `hex-ring-2.csv` are deleted, and `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` (the CSV parity test) is removed or replaced by a test that pins the generator as the single source.
- No runtime scene imports authored ring content: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` obtain their definitions from the seed-aware source, and `PlayScene`'s `findHexRingDefinition(hexId)` deployment lookup resolves through it.
- Fixtures and harnesses are migrated, not deleted where they still carry value: `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringFixtures.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/aggressionScenarios.ts` and `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` derive their sample rings from the generator for rings 1–3 (a deliberately pinned seed may replace hand-authored variety samples; any hand-authored fixture that no longer has a rationale is removed rather than left orphaned).
- Every test that imported `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` / `hexRingDefinitionsFor` / `findHexRingDefinition` is migrated to the generator (21 test files currently import them; the AST/`grep` check for authored ring imports across `src/` (excluding test fixtures) is empty).
- The published map promise is unchanged: the map scene still renders boss, strengths/weaknesses, aggression and grant per hex, and the `6 × n` geometry is untouched.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- **Blast radius is the main risk:** 21 test files and the four scenes import
  the authored symbols today. Migrate by capability, not by symbol-renaming, and
  keep each file's assertions meaningful (do not delete coverage to make the
  build pass).
- The variety coverage that lived in hand-authored ring-1/ring-2 rows
  (personality, contract, fortress landmark) must still be exercised: keep at
  least one variety assertion per axis against a pinned seed that produces it,
  or state explicitly in the item's completion comment why an axis is no longer
  reachable.
- Retirement must not change the `6 × n` geometry or the one-weapon-hex/one-
  special-mission publishing rules.

**Key Files:**

- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — retire the authored table (keep only vocabulary exports the generator draws from, if any).
- `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv`, `src/data/hex-ring-2.csv` — delete the seeds.
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` — remove or replace the CSV parity test.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — remove the authored default and the by-id authored lookup.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — use the seed-aware definitions source.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — same, including the ring-1 weapon-hex definition the HEX control uses.
- `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringFixtures.ts` — derive fixtures from the generator.
- `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/aggressionScenarios.ts` — replace the synthesised "ring 3+" shape with the real generator.
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` — resolve ring definitions from the generator.

## Related work

- Parent **AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA** — Procedurally generated Hex Map (epic); Q1 = B
  producer decision (all rings procedural).
- **AH-0MVUXC9KG008G80Y** — created the authored table this item retires.

# Save compatibility for generated rings

## Goal

Guarantee that switching the content source to a generator cannot damage an
existing war save: a stored ring is preserved byte-for-byte and a fresh ring
generates.

**User story:** As a player, loading my existing war keeps exactly the map I
have been playing, and starting a war (or opening a ring) gives me a generated
map that survives reload unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Existing saves remain playable and unchanged**: a stored ring (full or partial) is never regenerated or discarded; a fresh/empty ring generates from the seed; defensive parse and migration behaviour is covered by tests.
- A payload written before this change (authored ring hexes, ids `hex-r1-*` / `hex-r2-*`, a stored `frontierTick`, absent `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels`) loads and round-trips unchanged: every hex id, coordinate, held state, aggression and defender is byte-for-byte identical after a save/load cycle, with no schema version bump.
- A partial ring (some hexes stored, fewer than the full ring) is preserved exactly and is never padded up to the generated ring's size; the next ring opened is generated from the seed.
- A fresh or empty ring generates from `payload.seed` and round-trips: save → load → the same generated hexes (no re-roll on reload), because generation is a pure function of the persisted seed and ring index.
- Defensive parse behaviour is asserted: a corrupt or absent `seed`, a non-object ring, a malformed hex row and an unknown extra field all degrade to a playable payload (or a clean null) rather than throwing, matching `parseHangarWarPayload`'s existing contract.
- Migration coverage is explicit in tests for: legacy authored payload, fresh payload, partial ring, corrupt ring, and large ring index (e.g. ring 7) round-trip.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- No schema change is intended (producer Q2 = A): the seed and `ring.ringIndex`
  are the only generation inputs and both are already persisted. If an
  implementation detail makes a new field unavoidable, it must be additive,
  optional and migrated by field presence — and that deviation must be recorded
  in the item's completion comment.
- The stored-ring invariant is the safety property: generation may only fill an
  **empty** ring, never rewrite a non-empty one.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — `parseHangarWarPayload`, `createDefaultPayload`, `loadHangarWarPayload` / `saveHangarWarPayload` (field-presence migration, no version bump).
- `src/core/hangarWar/storage.ts` — the storage seam the round-trip tests drive.
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HangarWarPayload` / `HexState` field presence rules.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts` — parse/migration tests to extend.
- `src/core/hangarWar/storage.test.ts` — save/load round-trip tests to extend.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — `materialiseRing`'s stored-ring invariant (the behaviour under test).

## Related work

- Parent **AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA** — Procedurally generated Hex Map (epic); Q2 = A
  producer decision (pure function of `(payload.seed, ringIndex)`, generated on
  demand; only `HexState` persisted).
- **AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ** — the defender upgrade snapshot: the precedented
  additive/optional field-presence migration pattern to follow.
- **AH-0MWHW4ALS0039JFU** — the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` optional fields
  an old payload legitimately lacks.

# Gym and game parity for generated rings

## Goal

Prove the gym and the game render and resolve exactly the same generated ring,
so the headless harness is trustworthy evidence for a seed-derived map.

**User story:** As a test/agent, `GymHexWar` renders the same generated model as
the game, so what I measure in the gym is what the player plays.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit, property and integration tests cover determinism, distinct-seed variety, invariant enforcement across many seeds and large ring indices, the grant-economy rule, and the save/load round-trip; `GymHexWar` renders the same generated model as the game.
- `GymHexWar` obtains its ring definitions from the same seed-aware source as the game (no gym-only authored fixture), and an explicit parity test asserts the gym and game read models are deep-equal for at least three seeds and ring indices 1, 2 and 3.
- `GymMiniBoss`'s HEX control resolves its deployment definition (the ring's weapon hex) from the generator for the payload's seed and ring index, so the boss body colour and opening volley come from the generated weapon hex rather than `hex-r1-6` fixture data.
- A parity assertion covers the intel read model (boss, strengths/weaknesses, aggression, grant) and the weapon-hex/special-mission flags, so a gym-only divergence fails loudly.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`'s hex-ring rows are updated to describe the generated source and the new parity test as the evidence column (the docs sweep item may polish wording; this item's row must be accurate).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- Parity means the same **pure read model**, not pixel equality: both sides call
  `buildHexMapModel` with definitions from the same source and the same payload.
- This item is the epic's gym↔game evidence gate; it must not introduce a
  gym-only code path to make the comparison pass.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — the gym ring definitions source.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — the HEX control's deployment definition.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts` — add the gym↔game parity assertions.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.test.ts` — HEX control definition assertions.

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — `buildHexMapModel`, the read model both sides render.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — the parity table rows for the hex ring.

- Parent **AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA** — Procedurally generated Hex Map (epic).

  precedent for this parity item's shape and evidence.

# Docs: procedural ring generation

## Goal

Update every document and code comment that still describes the authored
ring-content table, so the documented design of record is the seeded generator.

**User story:** As a designer or agent, the documentation says the ring is
generated from `(seed, ringIndex)` and no doc still tells me to author a table
per ring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` no longer describes the authored ring table or the CSV parity seeds as the content source; it states the pure `(seed, ringIndex)` generation rule, the design invariants the generator validates, and the grant level-scaling repeat rule (Q3 = A).
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D's "authored ring 1 / ring 2" framing is updated to the generated frontier with no authored ceiling, keeping the known-ahead intel promise and the `6 × n` shape intact.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md` and `README.md` references to the authored rings, the CSV seeds or the ring-2 ceiling are corrected, and `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` / `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` / `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts` module comments describe generation rather than authorship.
- Any doc that told a designer how to add a ring by appending authored rows is replaced with the generator's contract (draw order is versioned; changing it re-rolls every seed's map).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes

- Documentation must describe shipped behaviour, not aspiration: land this item
  after the generator, retirement and grant-economy items so every statement can
  be verified against the code.
- Keep the docs-site/wiki parity rule in mind: if a doc is generated or
  mirrored elsewhere in the repo, update the source rather than the mirror.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — the design of record sections naming the authored ring data and CSV seeds.

Fallback, per the parent's AC: if the ceiling cannot be reached without a churn regression, the highest achieved figures are recorded, the guard is pinned to them, and the residual gap is filed as a linked balance item — the measured result stands.

data.description:
The promo compiler joins every cut with a hard jump cut; it should dissolve between clips instead.

`npm run capture:promo` (`scripts/compile-promo.mjs`) turns the captured pool into a promo, a showreel and highlight clips by trimming and **concatenating** segments. Every junction in that concatenation is an instantaneous cut (`[v0][a0][v1][a1]concat=n=N:v=1:a=1`), so a ~40-cut promo reads as a strobe of hard cuts rather than an edited trailer. The producer wants the same cuts, joined by short cross-fades — a **400 ms** dissolve from the outgoing cut into the incoming one, with the audio cross-fading over a slightly longer **500 ms** — so the assembled package looks deliberately edited rather than spliced.

## Problem statement

The promo/showreel joins are hard `concat` boundaries with no transition, which reads as an unedited splice of separate recordings. A short dissolve at each junction (400 ms video) with a slower, slightly overlapping audio cross-fade (500 ms) would make the assembled package read as one continuous piece of marketing footage.

## Users

- **Producer / release owner** (primary) — publishes the compiled promo, showreel and highlight clips; wants the assembled package to look edited, not spliced.
  - *As a producer, I want each cut in the promo to dissolve into the next, with the sound blending a little more slowly than the picture, so the package looks and sounds edited rather than stitched together from separate recordings.*
- **Release engineer running `npm run capture:promo`** — needs the change to stay inside the existing contract: deterministic commands, the §7.6 pace/black-ratio gates, and the 45–60 s promo band.
  - *As a release engineer, I want the cross-fade timings to be configurable editorial knobs with the durations and gates verified from the delivered files, so a recompile is reproducible and still passes validation.*
- **Agent implementing/auditing the compiler** — needs the junction rule expressed once (in `EDITORIAL_CONFIG`) with tests, and needs audio/video timelines to stay aligned (no accumulating drift) rather than being fixed by ear.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Multi-cut deliverables join their cuts with a **dissolve**, not a hard cut: the `-filter_complex` graph built by `buildDeliverableArgv` uses `xfade` (video) and `acrossfade` (audio) between consecutive streams, with no `concat` filter remaining on the multi-cut path. Promo **and** showreel both cross-fade; single-cut highlights are unchanged.
- The transition durations are frozen editorial knobs in `EDITORIAL_CONFIG` — video dissolve **400 ms**, audio cross-fade **500 ms**, both clamped to at most a quarter of the shorter neighbouring cut — read through shared derived exports, and setting the video duration to `0` restores the current hard-cut `concat` graph byte-for-byte so the change is opt-outable.
- **Audio and video stay aligned across the whole deliverable** with no cumulative drift: because the audio cross-fade overlaps 100 ms more than the picture at every junction, the audio chain is compensated per junction (the outgoing cut's audio is extended by the extra overlap from its source headroom, or the junction's audio fade is deterministically clamped back to the video duration when that headroom does not exist), so the delivered audio and video streams end within one frame of each other rather than the audio running short by `100 ms × (junctions − 1)`.
- Each deliverable's expected duration — `Σ cut durations − Σ video transitions` — is computed in the plan/command layer, uses the same arithmetic to size the promo fill budget so a delivered promo still measures inside the 45–60 s band (§7.6), and is recorded in the compile report alongside the configured transition settings (so expected-vs-measured is auditable).
- Cross-fading does not break the existing delivery gates: the dissolve is between the two cuts (never through black) so the ≥ 0.90 non-black ratio gate still holds, and the §7.6 pace band passes on a real compile.
- Unit tests cover: cross-faded graph shape for a multi-cut deliverable, chained offset arithmetic, per-junction clamping on short cuts, the 500/400 ms audio-video alignment compensation (including the no-headroom fallback) with no accumulating drift, the `0`-duration hard-cut regression, single-segment output unchanged, and byte-identical argv for an identical plan (the existing determinism test must keep passing).
- The gated real-ffmpeg smoke test (`scripts/compile-promo.e2e.test.ts`, `--project e2e`) proves a real ffmpeg accepts the cross-faded command line and yields a probe-able VP9/Opus WebM whose video and audio durations match the expected `Σ cuts − Σ fades` (within its existing tolerance) and each other.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code comments, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (compiling a promo package), `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.6 (duration/fill accounting), the `--help` text, and `README.md` where the promo package is described.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The compiled promo and showreel dissolve from cut to cut with a slightly slower audio blend instead of hard-cutting, so the published footage looks and sounds like an edited trailer rather than a splice of separate recordings.

## Constraints

- **Deterministic output stays a hard requirement:** the same plan + probes must still produce byte-identical ffmpeg argv (existing regression test `ffmpeg driver — deterministic command building`). Transition offsets and audio compensation must therefore be derived from the plan's `videoInMs`/`videoOutMs` and the probed source durations only — never from wall-clock or encoder state.
- **A/V alignment is not negotiable:** a longer audio cross-fade must not shorten the audio timeline relative to the picture (that becomes audible desync, growing with cut count). The compensation rule must be explicit in code and tested, not tuned by inspection.
- **Existing gates are not lowered:** `EDITORIAL_CONFIG.targets` (promo 45–60 s, showreel > 2 min, 5 highlights), the §7.6 pace band and the ≥ 0.90 non-black ratio stay as they are; cross-fades must be fitted to them, not waived for them.
- **Re-encode cost:** `xfade`/`acrossfade` add decode work to a pass that is already the pipeline's slow step (the e2e smoke test costs ~140 s on a ~5 s fixture). No extra encode pass may be introduced — the dissolve and the audio blend must live inside the existing single `-filter_complex` pass.
- **ffmpeg build:** the host's ffmpeg is already required to carry VP9 + Opus; `xfade`/`acrossfade` are standard filters, but the prerequisite check/message and docs may need a note if an older build is found.
- **Scope:** transition variants beyond a dissolve (dips to black, wipes, zoom transitions, per-category transition choice) are out of scope — record them as follow-up work items instead of widening this one.

## Existing state

- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` builds every command in `buildDeliverableArgv` (`~L1578`): per-input trim/normalise chains (`[i:v]trim=…,scale=…,fps=…[vi]`, `[i:a]atrim=…[ai]`), then either a pass-through map for a single segment or `concat=n=N:v=1:a=1[v][a]` for many. Video and audio lengths are identical today, which is why a hard cut never desyncs.
- The plan's fill budget reserves measured encode overhead only — `promoBudgetMs = targets.promo.maxMs − targets.promo.safetyMs` (`~L757`) — and sums nominal cut lengths, which currently equals delivered length because a hard `concat` loses nothing.
- Validation measures the **delivered** files: `assessDeliverable` (probe + brightness) and `assessTargets` (promo/showreel/highlight sizes) feed `capture-output/compile-promo-report.json` and gate `npm run capture:promo`'s exit code. Source durations are probed and segments already clamped to them in `buildDeliverableCommands`, so per-junction audio headroom is knowable before the graph is built.
- `EDITORIAL_CONFIG` (`~L109`) is the single frozen home for editorial knobs (`categories`, `targets`, `highlightKnobs`, `dedupeTolerances`, `paceBand`, `cutCadence`) with derived exports; all of them are asserted against the config in derivation tests.
- There is currently **no** transition/`xfade` code anywhere in the repo (grep for `xfade|acrossfade` finds no production or test usage).

## Desired change

1. Add a frozen `transitions` block to `EDITORIAL_CONFIG` — `{ videoFadeMs: 400, audioFadeMs: 500, maxFadeRatio: 0.25 }` — plus derived exports, documented as the editorial knobs for junction style.
2. Build the junction chain in `buildDeliverableArgv`: fold normalised `[v0..vn]` through successive `xfade=transition=fade:duration=0.4:offset=O` steps and `[a0..an]` through `acrossfade=d=0.5`, computing each video offset from cumulative nominal cut durations minus elapsed transition time. Keep the single-segment path and the zero-duration path exactly as they are.
3. Compensate the audio timeline per junction so the extra `audioFadeMs − videoFadeMs` (100 ms) of audio overlap does not shorten the audio: extend the outgoing cut's audio tail by that amount from available source headroom (the already-probed duration beyond `videoOutMs`), and where headroom is short, clamp that junction's audio fade to `videoFadeMs + availableHeadroom` — deterministically, from plan + probe values only. Result: audio and video totals agree within one frame at any cut count.
4. Compute each deliverable's expected duration from the same arithmetic, feed it into the promo fill budget (so overlap is accounted for *before* filling) and expose it in the command/report objects, so the compile summary and `compile-promo-report.json` state expected duration and transition settings next to the measured ones.
5. Update the `--help` text, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.6 and `README.md`.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — `EDITORIAL_CONFIG` (add `transitions`), `buildDeliverableArgv` (xfade/acrossfade chain, offsets, audio alignment compensation, expected duration), `buildEditPlan` promo fill budget (~L757), `buildDeliverableCommands` (source headroom for compensation), `compileDeliverables` report fields, `USAGE_TEXT`.
- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` — cross-fade graph shape, offset arithmetic, short-cut clamping, 500/400 ms alignment no-drift + no-headroom fallback, zero-duration regression, single-segment unchanged, determinism.
- `scripts/compile-promo.e2e.test.ts` — real-ffmpeg acceptance of the cross-faded graph; delivered video/audio durations match the expectation and each other.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — "Compiling a promo package" gains the transition behaviour and the audio alignment rule.
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — §7.6 duration/fill accounting note (dissolve, not fade-to-black).
- `README.md` — promo package description.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVDV4PNZ004ZWOZ** — ffmpeg compile driver and output validation (completed): owns `buildDeliverableArgv`/`compileDeliverables`, i.e. the code this item changes.
- **AH-0MVDV50Z20071RF4** — Produce and validate the promo, showreel and highlight clips (completed): the deliverable targets and pace band the transition must not break.
- **AH-0MVDV4OKN001OT18** — Implement: pure edit-plan and selection logic in compile-promo (completed): owns `buildEditPlan`, where the promo fill budget lives.
- Automated find-related report: 3 related work items and 3 repository matches (`docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `README.md`); duplicate check performed — no completed item implements transitions.
- Editorially adjacent history (not overlapping): AH-0MVSDM8SE0081WU7 / AH-0MVSDMBU60018JOE (promo scenarios), AH-0MW44FQTW007YDGH (scenario recalibration).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Confirmed (Q1):** promo **and** showreel cross-fade; single-cut highlights are untouched (no junction to fade).
- **Confirmed (Q2):** 400 ms dissolve, clamped to ≤ 25 % of the shorter neighbouring cut. Very short cuts (`CUT_CADENCE.maxCutMs` = 6 s, and folded remainders may be shorter) would otherwise be swallowed by their own transition.
- **Confirmed (Q3):** audio cross-fades with the picture, deliberately slower at 500 ms. This is the item's main technical risk — see next bullet.
- **Risk — A/V drift:** a 500 ms audio cross-fade against a 400 ms video dissolve removes 100 ms more audio per junction; uncompensated, ~40 junctions leave the audio ≈ 3.9 s short of the picture, which is unusable. Mitigation: per-junction audio tail extension from source headroom with a deterministic clamp fallback, plus a unit test asserting no accumulating drift and an e2e assertion that delivered audio ≈ video duration.
- **Risk — headroom availability:** cuts that end at (or near) the source's end have no tail to extend, so their audio fade falls back to the video duration. Mitigation: deterministic, per-junction, documented — never a global setting change.
- **Risk — duration drift on the video side:** every junction removes 400 ms from the total, so a heavily cut promo can lose 10–20 s; without the fill-budget fix it would drop under the 45 s floor and fail `assessTargets`. Mitigation: compute expected duration first (net of fades), then fill against it, and keep the report's expected-vs-measured pair.
- **Risk — cadence/pacing:** dissolving on cuts as short as 1–2 s can soften the "peak per cut" punch the pace band measures. Mitigation: the 25 % clamp plus keeping the transition shorter than each cut's leading action peak; if the measured pace band regresses, shrink `videoFadeMs` rather than lowering the band.
- **Risk — graph complexity:** `xfade` requires matching timebase/format/fps across inputs; the existing per-input normalisation (`fps`, `format=yuv420p`, `setsar=1`, `setpts`) already provides it, so those steps must stay ahead of the fade chain.
- **Risk — encode time:** an added filter pass on ~40 cuts lengthens an already slow compile; mitigated by keeping it the *same* pass (no extra encode) and the e2e smoke test gated to `--project e2e`.
- **Scope-creep guard:** transition variants (wipes, dip-to-black, per-category transition choice) are out of scope and should be filed as their own items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "**Q1. Which deliverables should cross-fade?** — A) promo only, B) promo + showreel (highlights are single-cut), C) every multi-cut deliverable. **Recommended:** B — the showreel is the same footage joined the same way." — **Answer (Producer, interactive reply, this session): "B"** — promo and showreel cross-fade; single-cut highlights unchanged. Source: work-item comment on AH-0MWLYWYGK004JR2A + producer reply.
- Q: "**Q2. How long should each cross-fade be?** — A) 300 ms, B) 400 ms clamped to ≤ 25 % of the shorter neighbouring cut, C) 600 ms, D) adaptive. **Recommended:** B." — **Answer (Producer, interactive reply, this session): "B"** — 400 ms video dissolve with the 25 % clamp. Source: work-item comment on AH-0MWLYWYGK004JR2A + producer reply.
- Q: "**Q3. What happens to the audio at each junction?** — A) cross-fade audio with the picture (`acrossfade`), B) hard audio cuts. **Recommended:** A." — **Answer (Producer, interactive reply, this session): "A (audio cross fade should be slightly slower than the video, e.g. 500ms)"** — audio cross-fades with the picture at 500 ms; the 100 ms excess overlap per junction is compensated per junction so the audio timeline is not shortened relative to the picture (see AC "Audio and video stay aligned"). Source: work-item comment on AH-0MWLYWYGK004JR2A + producer reply.
- Research (answered from the repo, no producer input needed): the junction is a single `concat` filter in `buildDeliverableArgv`; the promo fill budget is `maxMs − safetyMs` against nominal cut lengths; delivered duration is validated from the probed files by `assessTargets`; the ≥ 0.90 non-black band is measured from the delivered file (`docs/dev/action-intensity.md` §7.6); source durations are probed before the graph is built, so per-junction audio headroom is derivable deterministically; no `xfade`/`acrossfade` usage exists in the repo today. Sources: `scripts/compile-promo.mjs`, `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts`, `scripts/compile-promo.e2e.test.ts`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `docs/dev/action-intensity.md`.
- Duplicate check: `wl search "promo"`, `wl search "promo compile crossfade transition"` — no open or completed item implements cross-faded junctions; the three related completed items are the code the change lands in. Automated find-related report included above.

# Weak/Resist on hangar equip is misleading

## Problem statement

The target-aware config (hangar) screen marks **every** weapon row with its
matchup against the chosen hex's boss — green `▲ EFFECTIVE` when the boss is
weak to it, red `▼ RESISTED` when the boss resists it — but it does so even for
rows the player **cannot act on**: weapons they cannot buy (short of salvage,
`NEED 40 min`, or still ring-gated, `RING 2`) and owned weapons whose pricey
upgrade they cannot afford. Highlighting a recommendation the player cannot act
on reads as "buy this", so the intel lies about what is available right now.

## Users

- **The new player with no salvage** — "I have 0 minerals; every weapon row is
  lit up as if I could bring or upgrade it. Only light up what I can act on."
- **The ring-1 player** — "A ring-2 weapon is shown in bright red as if my
  loadout choice matters; I cannot buy it yet."
- **The accessibility-minded player** — "The matchup must still be readable
  without colour wherever it is shown." (Repo CVD policy: never colour-only.)
- **The producer/maintainer** — "One shared model decides the highlight, so the
  game and `GymHangar` cannot drift and no scene owns a second rule."

Example user stories:

- As a player with no salvage, I still read the boss's intel and the `▲`/`▼`
  verdicts, but only the rows I could actually buy or upgrade are highlighted.
- As a player with enough salvage for one weapon, that row is highlighted and
  the ones I cannot afford render as ordinary disabled rows.
- As a player equipping a weapon I already own, the `LOADOUT` column keeps its
  full matchup highlight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Rows with no available action are not highlighted.** In the hangar screen's
  unlock tree, a `weapon` row the player cannot act on right now — purchase
  states `unaffordable` (`NEED … min`) and `gated` (`RING n`), and upgrade
  states `upgrade-unaffordable` and `capped` (`MAX`) — renders with **no**
  strong/weak colour and **no** strong/weak background tint, keeping the
  ordinary row styling (muted colour, its price/shortfall or `MAX` intact).
- **Rows with an available action keep their highlight.** A `weapon` row whose
  own action is available — a `buyable` purchase row and an `upgradable` upgrade
  row — keeps exactly today's behaviour: `▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED` marker,
  strong/weak colour and tint.
- **The `LOADOUT` column is unchanged.** Every starting-weapon row in the
  deployment selector (owned weapons, always toggleable) keeps its marker,
  colour and tint, because equipping/unequipping it is always available.
- **The marker stays on every weapon row.** The `▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED`
  text tag is appended wherever the weapon has a strong/weak verdict, including
  the non-highlighted rows, so the intel stays readable without colour (CVD
  policy) and only the colour/tint follows affordability.
- **The shared model decides, and the gym agrees.** Whether a row is highlighted
  is published by `buildHangarScreenModel`/`buildHangarUnlockRows` (data beside
  the existing `matchup` verdict), never derived from the render-time
  interactive/actionable flag, so the read-only `GymHangar` render shows exactly
  the game's highlight; a test asserts the model, the game render and the gym
  render agree for the same payload.
- **Automated tests cover the matrix.** Model-level and render-level tests for
  `buyable` + strong/weak, `unaffordable` + strong/weak, `gated` + strong/weak,
  `upgradable` + strong/weak, `upgrade-unaffordable` + strong/weak, `capped` +
  strong/weak, and a `LOADOUT` row of each strength; plus a test that a
  non-highlighted row keeps its marker, price and shortfall.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
  (`docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, GDD §8.2, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`).
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A player choosing a loadout only sees the boss-counter highlight on weapon rows
they can actually act on right now, while the `▲`/`▼` intel stays readable
everywhere — so the green/red marks are a promise the player can keep.

## Assumptions (documented; producer may override at review)

- **A1 — "Cannot buy" = `unaffordable` or `gated`.** Both mean the purchase
  cannot happen now (`canBuy` returns `unaffordable` for a salvage shortfall and
  `gated` for a not-yet-reached ring), so neither row is highlighted.
  (Producer Q2 = (a).)
- **A2 — Marker retained, colour suppressed.** A non-highlighted row keeps the
  `▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED` text marker and only loses the colour and backing
  tint, so it reads as a normal row whose matchup is still legible without
  colour. (Producer Q1 = (a).)
- **A3 — LOADOUT yes, upgrade tree no.** The `LOADOUT` equipped/unequipped column
  keeps its highlight for owned weapons (the action is always available); in the
  main upgrade/purchase tree the highlight follows the row's **own** action, so
  an owned weapon whose upgrade is `upgrade-unaffordable` (or `capped`) is **not**
  highlighted, while an `upgradable` one is. (Producer Q3: "equipped/unequipped
  column yes, main selection for upgrade no".)
- **A3.1 — `capped` (`MAX`) counts as "no available action".** A maxed row has
  nothing left to buy, so it is not highlighted; the player still sees the
  weapon highlighted in the `LOADOUT` column. Recorded as an OPEN QUESTION in
  case the producer would rather a maxed weapon keep its highlight.
- **A4 — Display only.** Prices, ring gating, ownership, the matchup resolver
  (`src/core/hangarWar/weaponMatchup.ts`) and the `TARGET INTEL` block are
  unchanged; this item changes only which rows are highlighted (parent
  AH-0MWMRWCY2001HWGR assumption A7 stands — the mechanical matchup is
  AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ).
- **A5 — No new persistence.** No payload schema or store change.
- **A6 — Existing fixtures must be re-baselined.** Today's matchup tests use a
  0-salvage payload whose weapons are all **owned**, so those rows are
  `upgrade-unaffordable` and (per A3) lose their colour: the rendered-colour
  assertion for `buy:spread` in `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` must change, and
  a fixture with salvage must be added to keep a positive highlight assertion.
  The `matchup` verdict and the `▲`/`▼` labels survive unchanged.

## Constraints

- **Model, not render, decides the highlight.** `renderHangarScreen` reports
  every row non-actionable in a read-only render (the gym), so keying the
  highlight off `actionable` would silently blank every mark in `GymHangar` and
  break gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`).
- **One shared code path.** No second matchup/highlight rule in `HangarScene`,
  `GymHangar` or the map; the pure model plus the one renderer stay the only
  place the rule lives.
- **Never colour-only.** The glyph tag stays on every weapon row with a verdict;
  a suppressed row must remain an ordinary readable row (price + shortfall, or
  `MAX`), not an unexplained blank.
- **No layout change.** No new rows or sections; `hangarLowestRowY` /
  bottom-row geometry are untouched.
- **No economy change.** The affordability verdicts are the economy's own
  (`canBuy`, `costToUpgrade`); this item only reads them.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Auto-buying the counter weapon, hiding non-weapon rows,
  dimming the `TARGET INTEL` block, or changing prices/gating are out of scope —
  record them as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Risks

- **Gym-parity regression (high).** Deriving the highlight from render-time
  `actionable` would blank every mark in the read-only gym; mitigated by
  publishing the decision in the model and asserting it in `GymHangar.test.ts`.
- **Test re-baseline churn (medium, expected).** Two existing tests assert a
  colour on rows that are now non-highlighted (0-salvage owned weapons); they
  must be updated deliberately, with a salvage-bearing fixture keeping the
  positive case covered.
- **Player surprise on `MAX` rows (low).** A maxed weapon loses its tree
  highlight (A3.1); the `LOADOUT` column still shows it, so the intel is never
  lost — flagged as an OPEN QUESTION for override.
- **Fixture blindness (medium).** No current fixture has a weapon it cannot
  afford, which is why this slipped through the parent epic; the new matrix adds
  one deliberately.

## Existing state

- `buildHangarUnlockRows` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) resolves a
  `matchup` for **every** `weapon`-kind row, regardless of the economy verdict,
  via `resolveBossMatchup(entry.weaponId, target)`, and appends the marker with
  `withMatchupMarker(...)`.
- The renderer's `rowColour(actionable, matchup)` returns
  `HANGAR_STRONG_COLOR` / `HANGAR_WEAK_COLOR` **before** consulting
  `actionable`, and `rowBackground(matchup)` tints the row — so an
  `unaffordable` (`NEED 40 min`), `gated` (`RING 2`), `upgrade-unaffordable` or
  `capped` (`MAX`) weapon row renders in the bright highlight colour with its
  tint even though nothing can be bought on it.
- `HangarUnlockRow.state` already carries the economy verdict (`owned`, `gated`,
  `unaffordable`, `buyable`, `upgradable`, `upgrade-unaffordable`, `capped`);
  the information needed is present, it is simply not consulted by the highlight.
- `HangarWeaponOption` rows are built from `unlockedWeapons` only (owned, always
  actionable), so the `LOADOUT` column is already always highlighted — and per
  A3 keeps that.
- `GymHangar` renders the same model with **no handlers**, so every rendered row
  reports `actionable: false` while showing the game's colours; the highlight
  must therefore be model data (`src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` pins parity).
- Tests today: `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` ("marks every weapon row …",
  "renders the intel section, the glyph tags and the matchup colours") and
  `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` ("renders the known target intel and ▲/▼
  matchup marks read-only") assert the marker/colour on rows from a 0-salvage
  fixture whose weapons are all **owned** (upgrade rows).

## Desired change

- **Publish the highlight decision in the model.** Beside `matchup`, expose
  whether that verdict should be *highlighted* for this row — true when the row's
  own action is available (`buyable` purchase, `upgradable` upgrade, and every
  `LOADOUT` weapon option), false for `unaffordable`, `gated`,
  `upgrade-unaffordable` and `capped` unlock rows — derived from the economy
  verdicts already on the row (no new economy rule).
- **Render from that flag.** `rowColour` / `rowBackground` consult the highlight
  flag (never the render-time `actionable` flag), so a non-highlighted row falls
  back to the existing row styling while highlighted rows keep today's colour
  and tint. The `▲`/`▼` marker keeps being appended unconditionally by
  `withMatchupMarker`.
- **Cover the matrix with tests** in `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` (model +
  render, with a salvage-bearing fixture for the positive cases) and the gym
  parity case in `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts`.
- **Update the docs** that promise the current unconditional marking
  (`README.md` hangar/hex-map paragraphs, GDD §8.2, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`,
  `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § *Known-ahead intel*).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — the per-row highlight flag in
  `buildHangarUnlockRows` / `buildHangarWeaponOptions`, and the colour/tint
  decision in `rowColour` / `rowBackground`.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` — model + render tests for the `buyable` /
  `unaffordable` / `gated` / `upgradable` / `upgrade-unaffordable` / `capped` /
  `LOADOUT` matrix, and the re-baselined colour assertion.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` — parity: the gym renders the same
  suppressed highlight for a non-actionable row.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — record the highlight rule for `GymHangar`.
- `README.md` — the hangar and hex-map paragraphs that describe the marks.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §8.2 config-screen intel paragraph.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — § *Known-ahead intel* (the config screen
  marks "each weapon row").

## Related work

- **AH-0MWMRWCY2001HWGR — When starting a Hex War battle show the ship config
  screen** (completed): the parent epic that introduced the target-aware config
  screen and the unconditional marks this item narrows (children
  AH-0MWMT4NJV001PX8Y pure resolver, AH-0MWMT4QXF0095CBN model/render,
  AH-0MWMT4STK001PSK4 gym parity + docs).
- **AH-0MWMT4NJV001PX8Y — Weapon-vs-boss matchup resolver** (completed): the
  pure `resolveBossMatchup` verdict this item presents differently — unchanged.
- **AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ — Make hex strengths and weaknesses matter in combat**
  (open): owns the mechanical matchup; this item stays display-only.
- **AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY — Post-MVP Hangar War: hull upgrade bays as a reward
  axis** (open): future economy surface; unaffected but must not inherit a
  misleading highlight.
- Automated find-related report also surfaced `README.md`, `docs/Game Design
  Document.md` and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` as keyword matches
  (documentation touch points).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Asked in-session of the producer; the item was flagged `needsProducerReview`
while the questions were open and is released on their answers.

- **Q1 — Should a non-highlighted weapon row also lose the ▲/▼ text marker, or
  only the colour/tint?**
  Options: (a) keep the marker, suppress colour + tint; (b) hide marker and
  colour together; (c) keep the marker in the muted colour with a `· LOCKED`
  suffix.
  **Recommended:** (a) — the item asks for colour to follow affordability, and
  keeping the tag preserves the CVD-safe intel the parent epic required.
  **Answer (producer): (a)** — keep the marker, suppress only the colour and the
  backing tint. Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-20 session. Now recorded as
  AC4 and assumption A2.
- **Q2 — Does "not able to buy" include ring-gated rows (`RING 2`), or only rows
  short of salvage (`NEED … min`)?**
  Options: (a) both; (b) only `unaffordable`.
  **Recommended:** (a) — a gated row is equally unbuyable now, and `canBuy`
  already reports it as `gated` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts:528`).
  **Answer (producer): (a)** — both, any row the player cannot buy now. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-11-20 session. Now recorded as AC1 and assumption A1.
- **Q3 — Do owned weapons keep their highlight when their *upgrade* is
  unaffordable or capped?**
  Options: (a) yes — ownership makes the weapon usable now; (b) no — mute the
  row.
  **Recommended:** (a) (ownership makes the weapon usable now).
  **Answer (producer): split — "if you mean in the equipped/unequipped column
  yes, if you mean in the main selection for upgrade, no."** So the `LOADOUT`
  equipped/unequipped column keeps the highlight for owned weapons, while the
  main purchase/upgrade tree highlights only rows whose own action is available
  (`buyable` / `upgradable`). Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-20 session.
  This **supersedes** the earlier recommended (a) and is recorded as AC3/AC2 and
  assumption A3. Research: the 0-salvage fixtures make those tree rows
  `upgrade-unaffordable`, so their rendered-colour assertions must be
  re-baselined (assumption A6).
- **Q3.1 — Does a `capped` (`MAX`) row count as "no available action"?**
  **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION (producer) — drafted as "yes, not highlighted"
  (A3.1), because the row has nothing left to buy while the `LOADOUT` column
  still shows the weapon's matchup highlighted. Overriding this only changes one
  state in the highlight predicate.
data.title: Weak/Resist on hangar equip is misleading

data.description:
# Intake Brief — Hangar: make owned power-ups installable in the deployment loadout

## Problem statement

A deployment currently installs **every** owned level-bearing power-up
automatically: `buildHangarDeployment` copies the whole
`hangarPermanentLevels(hangar).powerUps` list into `powerUpLevels`, and
`applyHangarWarDeployment` grants all of it (trimmed only by the shared
six-slot cap). Because `HangarLoadout` holds just `startingWeapons` and
`modifiers`, the hangar screen has no way to express *which* power-ups a
deployment installs — so a fleet that owns more counted kinds than the cap has
its build silently chosen for it by catalogue order.

## Users

- **Player preparing a deployment** — wants to curate the build for the
  upcoming hex.
  - *As a player, when I own five power-ups but want two of them installed
    alongside four weapons, I want to pick those two, so the six slots go to
    the kit I chose rather than to whatever I bought first.*
  - *As a player, I want the loadout I see on the hangar screen to be exactly
    the kit the run launches with, so I am not surprised mid-battle.*
- **Player with an existing save** — wants to keep flying what they flew
  before this feature, without re-fitting anything.
- **Designer / maintainer** — wants one selection model consumed by the game
  and `GymHangar`, reusing the shipped slot cap and permanent-grant seams, with
  no second power-up budget and no schema bump.

## Existing state (verified in code)

- **The model has no power-up slot.** `HangarLoadout`
  (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`) is `{ startingWeapons: string[]; modifiers:
  string[] }`; `DeployedShip` mirrors the same three fields (hull +
  `startingWeapons` + `modifiers`).
- **Every owned level-bearing power-up is auto-installed.**
  `buildHangarDeployment` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`) maps
  `levels.powerUps` wholesale into `powerUpLevels`;
  `applyHangarWarDeployment` then caps the combined weapons+power-up list
  through `capDropIdsToSlotPool` and grants each row through
  `grantPermanentPowerUp` / `grantPermanentWeapon` (one grant per level), so
  the leftover rows are dropped by cap order, not by player choice.
- **Persistence is field-presence tolerant.** `parseLoadout`
  (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`) rebuilds the loadout from known
  fields only and defaults a missing/wrong-shaped loadout to empty; the payload
  is versioned (`version: 1`) but the GDD documents "migration is decided by
  field presence", so a new optional field needs no version bump.
- **Resolution filters to owned entries.** `resolveActiveLoadout` /
  `equipLoadout` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) drop catalogue-unknown
  or unowned ids, so a corrupt save can never install an unowned power-up.
- **The selector is weapons + modifiers only.** `buildHangarScreenModel`
  produces `HangarWeaponOption` and `HangarModifierOption` rows
  (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) with `toggleHangarWeapon` /
  `toggleHangarModifier` handlers; `GymHangar` renders the same model
  read-only, so any new row appears in both.
- **Consumption spends hull, weapons and modifiers only.**
  `consumeDeployedShip` removes the flown hull, starting weapons and modifiers
  (plus their bought level rows) and resets `activeLoadout` to
  `{ startingWeapons: [], modifiers: [] }`; power-up level rows are **not**
  spent today.

## Desired change

- Add an optional power-up selection to `HangarLoadout` and mirror it on
  `DeployedShip`, `parseLoadout` and `equipLoadout` — no schema/version bump.
- Render owned, level-bearing power-ups as toggleable rows in the hangar
  deployment selector, with the same equipped/unequipped affordance as weapons,
  through a `toggleHangarPowerUp` handler that routes through `equipLoadout`.
- Resolve the selection in `buildHangarDeployment` (only the selected rows reach
  `powerUpLevels`) and keep `applyHangarWarDeployment`'s grant loop and
  six-slot trim as the single grant seam.
- Make the displayed loadout equal the granted loadout: apply the same
  `capDropIdsToSlotPool` trimming in the screen model and render
  non-admitted rows as blocked/non-actionable rather than silently differing.
- Expose the selection to the auto-loadout selector (parent
  AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD) so its "balanced variety" fill can include power-ups.
- Keep gym↔game parity: `GymHangar` renders the same model read-only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Owned level-bearing power-ups appear as toggleable rows in the hangar deployment selector, with a clear equipped/unequipped state.
- [ ] A deployment grants exactly the selected power-ups (and their permanent levels); deselected power-ups are not granted.
- [ ] The combined selected weapons + power-ups respect the shared six-slot cap, and the displayed loadout matches what the run grants.
- [ ] A save written before this feature (no selection field) deploys with the existing behaviour, with no schema bump.
- [ ] The auto-loadout selector can select power-ups once this lands.
- [ ] The game and `GymHangar` render from the same model.
- [ ] Automated tests cover the model, the resolve/grant path and the gym parity (including a red-first test for the new selection field and its default).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the GDD (§8.1 payload, six-slot loadout), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the shipped slot cap (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` via `capDropIdsToSlotPool`)
  and the shipped permanent-grant seams; no second power-up budget.
- Additive persisted field only, in the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels`
  pattern; empty/absent must stay legal and must not throw.
- Do not change power-up balance, the six-slot semantics, or which kinds carry
  a permanent level (consumables and field-pickup-only kinds stay unselectable).
- Installation is a loadout choice, not a new spend: the existing
  `consumeDeployedShip` rule is unchanged — a flown hull, starting weapons and
  modifiers are spent, and installed power-ups are not.
- No Phaser or storage access in the pure core/deployment modules; `GymHangar`
  stays read-only (no purchase/toggle handlers).

## Assumptions and decisions

- **A1 — Tri-state field.** The new field is optional: `undefined` (a save
  written before this feature) means "not chosen yet" and keeps today's
  behaviour (every owned level-bearing power-up installs); `[]` means a
  deliberate empty selection and installs none; a populated list installs
  exactly those ids. This keeps AC4 satisfiable while letting a player empty
  the selection — the same shape `HangarLoadout.startingWeapons` already has.
- **A2 — Selection is persisted in `activeLoadout`,** not as a parallel
  top-level field, so `resolveActiveLoadout` / `equipLoadout` remain the single
  ownership filter and a corrupt save cannot install an unowned power-up.
- **A3 — Display equals grant via the shared cap predicate,** applied in the
  model as well as at grant time; grant-time trimming stays as the backstop for
  launch data from another build.
- **A4 — Installed power-ups are not consumed** (see Constraints). Power-up
  levels are permanent purchases; spending them per sortie would be an economy
  change this item explicitly excludes.
- **A5 — No producer questions were needed:** the seed description, the parent
  item (AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD) and the code above resolve every open point; the
  four decisions above are documented for confirmation at review.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Display/grant drift** (the reason AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX existed): mitigated by
  A3 — one predicate (`capDropIdsToSlotPool`) drives both the model and the
  grant, with a test asserting the two sets are equal.
- **Retro-fitting existing saves:** a naive default of "select nothing" would
  strip power-ups from every existing player's next sortie. Mitigated by A1
  (`undefined` ⇒ today's behaviour) and a test on a pre-feature payload.
- **Consumption regression:** adding a field to `DeployedShip` /
  `HangarLoadout` touches `consumeDeployedShip`'s reset shape. Mitigated by
  keeping the consumption rule unchanged (A4) and asserting the reset keeps the
  new field well-formed.
- **Row-count/layout pressure:** the right column already lays out weapons and
  modifiers by index (`hangarRightColumnLayout`); extra rows change nothing
  semantically but must not overlap. Mitigated by layout tests at a full
  catalogue.
- **Scope creep:** boss-matchup colouring for power-ups, auto-fit heuristics,
  and per-battle power-up spending belong to other items (parent
  AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD / AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY). They are recorded there, not
  pulled into this one.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HangarLoadout` and `DeployedShip` gain the optional power-up selection.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — `resolveActiveLoadout` / `equipLoadout` filter the selection to owned, level-bearing ids; `consumeDeployedShip` reset shape stays valid.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — `parseLoadout` reads the field with presence-based defaulting (A1), no version bump.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — `buildHangarDeployment` resolves only the selected rows into `powerUpLevels`; `applyHangarWarDeployment` cap/grant seam unchanged.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — `HangarPowerUpOption` rows, cap-aware `buildHangarScreenModel`, `toggleHangarPowerUp`, keyboard/focus wiring and layout.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — the shared `capDropIdsToSlotPool` / level-bearing-kind predicates the model and the grant both use (no new budget).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` — parity: renders the same read-only model.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts` (or nearest equivalents), `src/test/sixSlotLoadoutFixtures.ts` — red-first coverage of the model, the resolve/grant path and the parity.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §8.1 payload field and the six-slot loadout section.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — the `GymHangar` row (guarded by `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`).
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — Candidate D loadout description, if it enumerates loadout fields.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD** — Automatically select strong weapons (parent; this
  item was spawned from producer decision Q2 = A to make power-ups
  installable, because the auto-fill can only choose from an installable set).
- **AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX** — Loadout can exceed the six-slot cap (completed;
  established the shared cap predicate used here).
- **AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9** — Hex War doesn't add initial loadout to slots
  (completed; established the `applyHangarWarDeployment` registry grant seam).
- **AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D** — default-empty loadout decision (an empty selection
  is a legal deployment — the precedent for A1's `[]` case).
- **AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH** — Persist permanent levels through store and grant
  seam (completed; the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` pattern this field
  follows).
- **AH-0MWB8VDU4007G1LQ** — Model the per-ring deployment loadout (completed).
- **AH-0MWKXPO5A007R5RB** — Power-up unlock-tree kind, owned set and authored
  entry (completed; the owned-set source the selector reads).
- **AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY** — Post-MVP Hangar War: hull upgrade bays as a reward
  axis (open; adjacent loadout work, not blocking).

## Impact

Players can curate which owned power-ups a deployment installs, so the loadout
they see is the loadout they fly.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q1 — Does the new selection default to "all owned" or "none" for existing
saves?**
Answer (derived from the seed brief, no producer round needed): **all owned**,
via an optional (`undefined`) field. Evidence: the seed description's "preserve
the current default behaviour for saves without the new field"; current
behaviour verified in `buildHangarDeployment` (`powerUpLevels:
levels.powerUps.map(...)`) and `applyHangarWarDeployment`. Research: a "none"
default would silently strip power-ups from every live save on the next
sortie, contradicting the explicit constraint. Related:
AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D (an *explicit* empty selection is still legal). Decision
recorded as assumption A1.

**Q2 — Does installing a power-up mean the fleet spends it on battle end, like
a weapon?**
Answer: **No.** `consumeDeployedShip` spends the hull, starting weapons and
modifiers (and their bought level rows) and never power-up level rows; power-ups
are permanent level purchases and the item's constraints forbid changing
power-up balance or economy. Decision recorded as assumption A4; the
consumption rule is left byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Q3 — Where does the selection live: a new top-level hangar field or inside
`HangarLoadout`?**
Answer: **inside `HangarLoadout`** (plus `DeployedShip`). Rationale:
`resolveActiveLoadout` / `equipLoadout` are the shipped ownership filters, so a
parallel field would need a second filter and could install an unowned
power-up. Decision recorded as assumption A2.

**Q4 — Does the six-slot cap get enforced at selection time, at grant time, or
both?**
Answer: **both, from one predicate.** `applyHangarWarDeployment` already trims
weapons+power-ups through `capDropIdsToSlotPool`
(AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX); the screen model must apply the same predicate so the
displayed loadout equals the granted loadout (AC3), with grant-time trimming
kept as the backstop for launch data from another build. Decision recorded as
assumption A3.

**Q5 — Which power-up kinds are selectable?**
Answer: only **level-bearing** kinds — the same set `powerUpLevels` already
carries. Consumables (charge pools) and field-pickup-only kinds carry no
permanent level and are excluded, per the existing doc comment on
`HangarWarDeployment.powerUpLevels` (AH-0MWI5AG1X0007XZH AC5). No new rule.

**Plan revision note (2026-11-20):** re-read during planning; Q1–Q5 and
assumptions A1–A5 are unchanged and were reused without a new producer
round. No question was re-asked and no entry was duplicated.

**Open questions for the producer:** none. Items Q1–Q5 are answered from the
seed brief, the parent item and the shipped code, and are recorded as
assumptions A1–A5 for confirmation at review.

## Plan

Decomposed into eight child features in dependency order — one red-first
contract suite, five implementation slices (model → deployment → screen model →
scene wiring, plus the auto-loadout seam), the gym-parity slice and a docs/suite
closure. Each child is a vertical slice carrying its own tests and docs touch.

| # | Child | Type | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Red-first tests: power-up loadout selection (AH-0MWOWO5WX005HKWY) | task | — |
| 2 | Power-up loadout field and persistence (AH-0MWOWO6IJ006X5CC) | feature | 1 |
| 3 | Deployment grants only selected power-ups (AH-0MWOWO753006K7NJ) | feature | 2 |
| 4 | Hangar model: power-up selector rows (AH-0MWOWO7VY005BOZA) | feature | 3 |
| 5 | Hangar scene: power-up wiring and layout (AH-0MWOWO8KG006K0WJ) | feature | 4 |
| 6 | GymHangar parity for power-up rows (AH-0MWOWO9AS003FWJI) | feature | 4 |
| 7 | Auto-loadout power-up selection seam (AH-0MWOWO9X2005PB1G) | feature | 2, 3 |
| 8 | Power-up loadout docs and suite gate (AH-0MWOWOAJL005RN6M) | docs | 5, 6 |

**Vertical-slice phasing:** children 2–6 each cut through the layers they touch
(pure model + store + tests; deployment + tests; screen model + tests; scene +
layout/focus tests; gym + parity docs + guard). Between phases the next child's
description is reviewed and updated before implementation. Docs that describe
final behaviour (GDD, candidate doc, module JSDoc) land last in child 8 rather
than being scattered.

**Reuse, not reinvention:** the shared cap predicate (`capDropIdsToSlotPool`,
AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX), the permanent-grant seam (`applyHangarWarDeployment`,
AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9), the ownership filter (`ownedEntriesOf` /
`resolveActiveLoadout`) and the payload's presence-based migration are consumed
unchanged — no second power-up budget, no schema bump.

**Sequencing note for child 5:** the right column currently holds hulls,
weapons, modifiers and the compact saved-build block, and no viewport guard
exists yet; child 5 owns the full-catalogue layout test and may reduce the row
step (an allowed fix inside that child) if the new section overflows.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-20T11:40Z — plan run (downtime dispatch): read the intake brief and
  verified the shipped seams in `types.ts`, `hangarWarStore.ts`,
  `hangarEconomy.ts`, `hangarDeployment.ts`, `hangarScreen.ts`, `slots.ts` and
  `GymHangar.ts`; created 8 child features in test-first dependency order;
  wired 9 blocking edges; ran the six automated review stages and the AC
  coverage review (100% of the parent's criteria covered by children, no
  auto-created children needed). No new producer questions: the intake's
  Appendix Q1–Q5 answers were reused rather than re-asked.

## Goal

Pin the power-up selection contract **red-first**, so every implementation child
in this plan turns a failing test green instead of inventing a rule. Scope is
tests only (plus the shared fixture the later children reuse); no production
behaviour changes here.

## Summary

A red-first contract suite for the optional power-up selection field, its
tri-state default, the ownership filter, the deployment grant and the
display-equals-grant invariant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Automated tests cover the model, the resolve/grant path and the gym parity (including a red-first test for the new selection field and its default).
- A red-first test suite covers the optional power-up selection field on `HangarLoadout` / `DeployedShip`, including its `undefined` default (a pre-feature payload keeps today's all-owned behaviour) and its `[]` (deliberate empty selection) case.
- Tests assert persistence reads the field by presence with no schema/version bump, and a save written before this feature (no selection field) round-trips byte-for-byte and still parses.
- Tests assert the resolve/equip path drops catalogue-unknown, unowned and non-level-bearing ids, so a corrupt save can never install an unowned power-up.
- Tests assert a deployment grants exactly the selected power-ups (and their permanent levels); deselected power-ups are not granted.
- Tests assert the combined selected weapons + power-ups respect the shared six-slot cap, and the displayed loadout matches what the run grants.
- Every new test fails for the intended reason before the implementation children land, with the red-first evidence recorded as a comment on this item.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Extend `src/test/sixSlotLoadoutFixtures.ts` with a fixture fleet owning more level-bearing power-ups than the cap allows.
2. Add the failing assertions to `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts` (presence default, round-trip, corrupt value) and `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts` (ownership/kind filter, consumption reset shape).
3. Add the failing assertions to `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.test.ts` (selected rows only, `undefined` ⇒ all owned, deselected absent) and `hangarDeployment.levels.test.ts` (per-level grants for the selected set).
4. Record the red run (via the test skill, changed scope) as a comment before the model child starts.

## Key Files

- `src/test/sixSlotLoadoutFixtures.ts` — shared fleet fixtures (owned sets, cap-bound loadouts).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts` — persistence default and round-trip.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts` — resolve/equip filter and consumption reset.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.test.ts` — selected rows, default behaviour.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.levels.test.ts` — per-level grant seam.

## Dependencies

None — this is the first child and every other child depends on it.

## Risks

- Writing assertions against an undesigned API name; keep names aligned with the sibling field (`startingWeapons`) and settle them here so later children do not churn.

## Goal

Give the loadout model a place to say **which** owned power-ups a deployment
installs, and persist it additively. Nothing grants anything different yet — this
child makes the selection expressible, validated and durable.

## Summary

Optional tri-state power-up selection on `HangarLoadout` / `DeployedShip`, read
by presence in the store and filtered to owned, level-bearing ids by the economy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `HangarLoadout` gains an optional power-up selection field and `DeployedShip` mirrors it; both stay additive and optional, so no schema or payload version bump is needed.
- Persistence reads the field by presence (assumption A1): absent stays `undefined`, a present list is read as ids, and a corrupt value collapses to an empty selection without throwing.
- A save written before this feature (no selection field) deploys with the existing behaviour and round-trips unchanged.
- The resolve/equip path filters the selection to owned, catalogue-known, level-bearing power-up ids, so a corrupt save can never install an unowned power-up.
- Consumption is unchanged: a flown hull, starting weapons and modifiers (plus their bought level rows) are spent, installed power-ups are not, and the reset `activeLoadout` stays well-formed.
- The red-first tests from the contract child pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `powerUps?: string[]` (or the settled name) to `HangarLoadout` and `DeployedShip` in `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`, with a JSDoc stating the tri-state rule.
2. Read it in `parseLoadout` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`) with presence-based defaulting beside `startingWeapons`/`modifiers`.
3. Filter it in `resolveActiveLoadout` / `equipLoadout` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) through the existing `ownedEntriesOf` helper with the `power-up` kind plus the level-bearing predicate.
4. Leave `consumeDeployedShip`'s reset shape byte-compatible for the new field and assert it.

## Key Files

- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HangarLoadout`, `DeployedShip`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — `parseLoadout` presence defaulting.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — `resolveActiveLoadout`, `equipLoadout`, `consumeDeployedShip`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts` — the tests made green.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the red-first contract tests (so the field is written against failing assertions, not invented).

## Risks

- A wrong default silently strips power-ups from every live save; pinned by the pre-feature-payload test.
- A second ownership rule could install an unowned power-up; avoided by reusing `ownedEntriesOf`.

## Goal

Make the deployment launch exactly the power-ups the loadout selects, keeping
the shipped grant seam and six-slot cap as the only budget.

## Summary

`buildHangarDeployment` resolves only the selected rows into `powerUpLevels`;
`applyHangarWarDeployment`'s cap/grant loop stays the single grant seam.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A deployment grants exactly the selected power-ups (and their permanent levels); deselected power-ups are not granted.
- An absent selection (`undefined`) keeps today's behaviour — every owned level-bearing power-up is installed — so existing saves deploy unchanged.
- The deployment grant stays the single seam: `capDropIdsToSlotPool` plus `grantPermanentPowerUp` are reused unchanged, with no second power-up budget and no balance change.
- Grant-time trimming still applies as the backstop for launch data built by another build.
- The red-first deployment tests from the contract child pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Thread the resolved selection into `buildHangarDeployment` beside `resolveActiveLoadout`, mapping only the selected ids onto the persisted level rows.
2. When the field is `undefined`, fall back to the current wholesale map so the default path is byte-for-byte the old behaviour.
3. Leave `applyHangarWarDeployment` untouched (documented as the backstop) and assert its trim still bounds a selection that arrived over the cap.
4. Extend the deployment tests with the selected/unselected/absent trio.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — `buildHangarDeployment`, `applyHangarWarDeployment`.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.test.ts`, `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.levels.test.ts` — coverage.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — shared cap predicate (consumed, not changed).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the loadout model and persistence child (the selection must be expressible first).

## Risks

- Display/grant drift at the cap; mitigated by one predicate and an explicit equality test (extended in the screen-model child).
- Launch data from another build could over-select; the grant-time trim stays as the backstop.

## Goal

Put owned, level-bearing power-ups in the hangar's deployment selector, with the
same equipped/unequipped affordance as weapons, and make the shown loadout the
granted loadout.

## Summary

`HangarPowerUpOption` rows and a cap-aware model plus a pure `toggleHangarPowerUp`
updater beside `toggleHangarWeapon` / `toggleHangarModifier`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Owned level-bearing power-ups appear as toggleable rows in the hangar deployment selector, with a clear equipped/unequipped state.
- A pure `toggleHangarPowerUp` updater routes through the resolve/equip seam and returns a fresh payload (persisted by the caller), mirroring `toggleHangarWeapon`.
- The combined selected weapons + power-ups respect the shared six-slot cap, and the displayed loadout matches what the run grants: the model applies the same cap predicate as the grant, and non-admitted rows render blocked/non-actionable rather than silently differing.
- Power-up kinds that carry no permanent level (consumables, field-pickup-only) never appear as rows.
- The new rows are registered in the model's `focusOrder` in reading order, and a non-actionable (blocked) row is never focusable.
- The red-first model tests from the contract child pass.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `HangarPowerUpOption` and a `powerUpOptions` array to `HangarScreenModel`, built from the owned id set filtered to level-bearing catalogue entries (`power-up` kind).
2. Compute the admitted set once with `capDropIdsToSlotPool` over weapons + power-ups and mark rows outside it `actionable: false` with a blocked label.
3. Add `toggleHangarPowerUp` beside the weapon/modifier toggles, going through `equipLoadout` so the ownership filter is the only gate.
4. Extend `focusOrder` and add the display-equals-grant equality test (model admitted set === `buildHangarDeployment` `powerUpLevels` ids).

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — option type, model builder, toggle updater, focus order.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — `capDropIdsToSlotPool` (consumed, not changed).
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarPurchaseEquip.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` — model/updater coverage.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the deployment resolution child (the grant contract the display must equal).
- Assumption A3: one shared cap predicate drives both the display and the grant.

## Risks

- The right column has no existing viewport guard; the layout child owns the
  no-overlap/full-catalogue sizing so this child stays model-only.
- Marker/ordering vocabulary is settled here by matching the weapons' affordance
  (`EQUIPPED` suffix plus a blocked variant); a designer preference would be a
  follow-up, not a blocker.
